Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Abhidhammapiṭake

In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka

Paṭṭhānapāḷi

The Book of Conditional Relations

(Paṭhamo bhāgo)

(First Part)

Dhammānulome

Positive Method

Tikapaṭṭhānaṃ

The Conditional Relations of the Triads

(1) Paccayuddeso

(1) Enumeration of Conditions

Hetupaccayo[T 1.0001][M 1.0001][V 1.0001], ārammaṇapaccayo, adhipatipaccayo, anantarapaccayo, samanantarapaccayo, sahajātapaccayo, aññamaññapaccayo, nissayapaccayo, upanissayapaccayo, purejātapaccayo, pacchājātapaccayo, āsevanapaccayo, kammapaccayo, vipākapaccayo, āhārapaccayo, indriyapaccayo, jhānapaccayo, maggapaccayo, sampayuttapaccayo, vippayuttapaccayo, atthipaccayo, natthipaccayo, vigatapaccayo, avigatapaccayoti.

Root condition, object condition, dominance condition, proximity condition, contiguity condition, co-nascence condition, reciprocity condition, dependence condition, strong support condition, pre-nascence condition, post-nascence condition, repetition condition, kamma condition, result condition, nutriment condition, faculty condition, jhāna condition, path condition, association condition, dissociation condition, presence condition, absence condition, disappearance condition, non-disappearance condition.

(2) Paccayaniddeso

(2) Analysis of Conditions

1. Hetupaccayoti [V 1.0002] – hetū hetusampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo paccayoti (syā.).

1. Root condition: The roots are a condition, by way of root condition, for states associated with the roots and for material phenomena originated therefrom.

2. Ārammaṇapaccayoti – rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Saddāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā [T 1.0002][M 1.0002] taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Gandhāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Rasāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ saddāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Sabbe dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo.

2. Object condition: The visible object is a condition, by way of object condition, for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The sound object is a condition, by way of object condition, for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The odor object is a condition, by way of object condition, for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The taste object is a condition, by way of object condition, for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The tactile object is a condition, by way of object condition, for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The visible object, sound object, odor object, taste object, and tactile object are a condition, by way of object condition, for the mind element and for the states associated with it. All phenomena are a condition, by way of object condition, for the mind-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.

Yaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ ārabbha ye ye dhammā uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā, te te dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo.

Whatever phenomena are taken as an object, and whatever states of mind and mental factors arise in dependence on them, those phenomena are a condition for those states by way of object condition.

3. Adhipatipaccayoti – chandādhipati chandasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Vīriyādhipati vīriyasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Cittādhipati cittasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Vīmaṃsādhipati vīmaṃsasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo.

3. Predominance condition: Predominant desire is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the states associated with desire and for the material phenomena originating therefrom. Predominant energy is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the states associated with energy and for the material phenomena originating therefrom. Predominant mind is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the states associated with mind and for the material phenomena originating therefrom. Predominant investigation is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the states associated with investigation and for the material phenomena originating therefrom.

Yaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ garuṃ katvā ye ye dhammā uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā, te te dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo.

Whatever phenomena are regarded as important, and whatever states of mind and mental factors arise in dependence on them, those phenomena are a condition for those states by way of predominance condition.

4. Anantarapaccayoti [T 1.0003] – cakkhuviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

4. Proximity condition: The eye-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind element and its associated states. The mind element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states.

Sotaviññāṇadhātu [V 1.0003] taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

The ear-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind element and its associated states. The mind element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states.

Ghānaviññāṇadhātu [M 1.0003] taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

The nose-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind element and its associated states. The mind element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states.

Jivhāviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

The tongue-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind element and its associated states. The mind element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states.

Kāyaviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

The body-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind element and its associated states. The mind element and its associated states are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states.

Purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ [T 1.0004] abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

The preceding wholesome states are a condition for the succeeding wholesome states by way of proximity condition. The preceding wholesome states are a condition for the succeeding indeterminate states by way of proximity condition.

Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

The preceding unwholesome states are a condition for the succeeding unwholesome states by way of proximity condition. The preceding unwholesome states are a condition for the succeeding indeterminate states by way of proximity condition.

Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

The preceding indeterminate states are a condition for the succeeding indeterminate states by way of proximity condition. The preceding indeterminate states are a condition for the succeeding wholesome states by way of proximity condition. The preceding indeterminate states are a condition for the succeeding unwholesome states by way of proximity condition.

Yesaṃ [V 1.0004] yesaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarā ye ye dhammā uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā, te te dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

Immediately after whichever phenomena, whichever mental and associated phenomena arise; those preceding phenomena are a condition for those succeeding phenomena by way of the proximity condition.

5. Samanantarapaccayoti – cakkhuviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

5. Contiguity condition: The eye-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition. The mind-element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition.

Sotaviññāṇadhātu [M 1.0004] taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

The ear-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition. The mind-element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition.

Ghāṇaviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo[T 1.0005]. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

The nose-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition. The mind-element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition.

Jivhāviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

The tongue-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition. The mind-element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition.

Kāyaviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo. Manodhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

The body-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition. The mind-element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the contiguity condition.

Purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

Preceding wholesome phenomena are a condition for subsequent wholesome phenomena by way of the contiguity condition. Preceding wholesome phenomena are a condition for subsequent indeterminate phenomena by way of the contiguity condition.

Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena [V 1.0005] paccayo. Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

Preceding unwholesome phenomena are a condition for subsequent unwholesome phenomena by way of the contiguity condition. Preceding unwholesome phenomena are a condition for subsequent indeterminate phenomena by way of the contiguity condition.

Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

Preceding indeterminate phenomena are a condition for subsequent indeterminate phenomena by way of the contiguity condition. Preceding indeterminate phenomena are a condition for subsequent wholesome phenomena by way of the contiguity condition. Preceding indeterminate phenomena are a condition for subsequent unwholesome phenomena by way of the contiguity condition.

Yesaṃ [T 1.0006] yesaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarā ye ye dhammā uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā, te te dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ samanantarapaccayena paccayo.

Immediately after whichever phenomena, whichever mental and associated phenomena arise; those preceding phenomena are a condition for those succeeding phenomena by way of the contiguity condition.

6. Sahajātapaccayoti [M 1.0005] – cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ kiñci kāle kañci kālaṃ (syā.) sahajātapaccayena paccayo, kiñci kāle na sahajātapaccayena paccayo.

6. Co-nascence condition: The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the co-nascence condition. The four great elements are a condition for one another by way of the co-nascence condition. At the moment of conception, name and form are a condition for one another by way of the co-nascence condition. Mental and associated phenomena are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the co-nascence condition. The great elements are a condition for derived material phenomena by way of the co-nascence condition. Material phenomena are sometimes a condition for immaterial phenomena by way of the co-nascence condition, and sometimes are not a condition by way of the co-nascence condition.

7. Aññamaññapaccayoti – cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo.

7. Mutuality condition: The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the mutuality condition. The four great elements are a condition for one another by way of the mutuality condition. At the moment of conception, name and form are a condition for one another by way of the mutuality condition.

8. Nissayapaccayoti – cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo.

8. Dependence condition: The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the dependence condition. The four great elements are a condition for one another by way of the dependence condition. At the moment of conception, name and form are a condition for one another by way of the dependence condition. Mental and associated phenomena are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the dependence condition. The great elements are a condition for derived material phenomena by way of the dependence condition.

Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ [T 1.0007] nissayapaccayena [V 1.0006] paccayo. Sotāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Ghānāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Jivhāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo.

The eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the dependence condition. The ear-base is a condition for the ear-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the dependence condition. The nose-base is a condition for the nose-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the dependence condition. The tongue-base is a condition for the tongue-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the dependence condition. The body-base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the dependence condition. That material form upon which the mind-element and the mind-consciousness element depend, that material form is a condition for the mind-element, the mind-consciousness element, and their associated states by way of the dependence condition.

9. Upanissayapaccayoti – purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā kusalā [M 1.0006] dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ kesañci upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo.

9. The strong dependence condition: Earlier wholesome states are a condition by way of strong dependence for later wholesome states. Earlier wholesome states are a condition by way of strong dependence for some later unwholesome states. Earlier wholesome states are a condition by way of strong dependence for later indeterminate states.

Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ kesañci upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo.

Earlier unwholesome states are a condition by way of strong dependence for later unwholesome states. Earlier unwholesome states are a condition by way of strong dependence for some later wholesome states. Earlier unwholesome states are a condition by way of strong dependence for later indeterminate states.

Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo[T 1.0008]. Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo.

Earlier indeterminate states are a condition by way of strong dependence for later indeterminate states. Earlier indeterminate states are a condition by way of strong dependence for later wholesome states. Earlier indeterminate states are a condition by way of strong dependence for later unwholesome states.

Utubhojanampi upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Puggalopi upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Senāsanampi upanissayapaccayena paccayo.

Climate and food are also a condition by way of strong dependence. Persons are also a condition by way of strong dependence. Dwellings are also a condition by way of strong dependence.

10. Purejātapaccayoti – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Sotāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ghānāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena [V 1.0007] paccayo. Jivhāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo.

10. The prenascence condition: The eye base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The ear base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The nose base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The tongue base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The body base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it.

Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Saddāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Gandhāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Rasāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ [M 1.0007] saddāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo.

The form base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The sound base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The odor base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The taste base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The tangible base is a condition by way of the prenascence condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it. The form base, sound base, odor base, taste base, and tangible base are conditions by way of the prenascence condition for the mind element and for the states associated with it.

Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu [T 1.0009] ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ kiñci kāle purejātapaccayena paccayo, kiñci kāle na purejātapaccayena paccayo.

The form on which the mind element and the mind-consciousness element depend is a condition for the mind element and for the states associated with it by way of the prenascence condition. For the mind-consciousness element and for the states associated with it, at times it is a condition by way of the prenascence condition, and at other times it is not a condition by way of the prenascence condition.

11. Pacchājātapaccayoti – pacchājātā cittacetasikā dhammā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo.

11. Postnascence condition: Subsequent mind and mental factors are a condition for this prenascent body by way of the postnascence condition.

12. Āsevanapaccayoti – purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā kiriyābyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo.

12. Repetition condition: Previous, previous wholesome states are a condition for subsequent, subsequent wholesome states by way of the repetition condition. Previous, previous unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent, subsequent unwholesome states by way of the repetition condition. Previous, previous functional indeterminate states are a condition for subsequent, subsequent functional indeterminate states by way of the repetition condition.

13. Kammapaccayoti – kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo.

13. Kamma condition: Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for resultant aggregates and for materiality produced by kamma by way of the kamma condition. Volition is a condition for the states associated with it and for the materiality arisen from it by way of the kamma condition.

14. Vipākapaccayoti [V 1.0008] – vipākā cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo.

14. Result condition: The four resultant immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the result condition.

15. Āhārapaccayoti – kabaḷīkāro kabaḷiṅkāro (ka. sī. syā.) āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. Arūpino āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo.

15. Nutriment condition: Material food is a condition for this body by way of the nutriment condition. Immaterial nutriments are conditions for the states associated with them and for the materiality arisen from them by way of the nutriment condition.

16. Indriyapaccayoti [T 1.0010] – cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Sotindriyaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Ghānindriyaṃ [M 1.0008] ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Jivhindriyaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo.

16. Faculty condition: The eye faculty is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and its associated mental states by way of the faculty condition. The ear faculty is a condition for the ear-consciousness element and its associated mental states by way of the faculty condition. The nose faculty is a condition for the nose-consciousness element and its associated mental states by way of the faculty condition. The tongue faculty is a condition for the tongue-consciousness element and its associated mental states by way of the faculty condition. The body faculty is a condition for the body-consciousness element and its associated mental states by way of the faculty condition. The material life faculty is a condition for materiality produced by kamma by way of the faculty condition.

Arūpino indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo.

Immaterial faculties are conditions for the mental states associated with them and for the materiality arisen from them by way of the faculty condition.

17. Jhānapaccayoti – jhānaṅgāni jhānasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo.

17. The jhāna condition: Jhāna factors are a condition for the states associated with jhāna and for the materiality originated thereby, by way of the jhāna condition.

18. Maggapaccayoti – maggaṅgāni maggasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo.

18. The path condition: Path factors are a condition for the states associated with the path and for the materiality originated thereby, by way of the path condition.

19. Sampayuttapaccayoti – cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo.

19. The associated condition: The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the associated condition.

20. Vippayuttapaccayoti – rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Arūpino dhammā rūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo.

20. The dissociated condition: Material phenomena are a condition for immaterial phenomena by way of the dissociated condition. Immaterial phenomena are a condition for material phenomena by way of the dissociated condition.

21. Atthipaccayoti [T 1.0011][V 1.0009] – cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo.

21. The presence condition: The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the presence condition. The four great elements are a condition for one another by way of the presence condition. At the moment of conception, name-and-form are a condition for one another by way of the presence condition. Consciousness and mental factors are a condition for materiality originated by consciousness by way of the presence condition. The great elements are a condition for derived materiality by way of the presence condition.

Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sotāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Ghānāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Jivhāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo.

The eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The ear-base is a condition for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The nose-base is a condition for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The tongue-base is a condition for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The body-base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition.

Rūpāyatanaṃ [M 1.0009] cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Saddāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Gandhāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Rasāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ saddāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo.

The form-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The sound-base is a condition for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The odor-base is a condition for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The taste-base is a condition for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The tangible-base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The form-base, sound-base, odor-base, taste-base, and tangible-base are a condition for the mind-element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition.

Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu [T 1.0012] ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo.

That material form depending on which the mind-element and the mind-consciousness-element arise, that material form is a condition for the mind-element, for the mind-consciousness-element, and for the states associated with them by way of the presence condition.

22. Natthipaccayoti – samanantaraniruddhā cittacetasikā dhammā paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ natthipaccayena paccayo.

22. The absence condition: Immediately ceased consciousness and mental factors are a condition for presently arisen consciousness and mental factors by way of the absence condition.

23. Vigatapaccayoti – samanantaravigatā cittacetasikā dhammā paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ vigatapaccayena paccayo.

23. The disappearance condition: Immediately disappeared consciousness and mental factors are a condition for presently arisen consciousness and mental factors by way of the disappearance condition.

24. Avigatapaccayoti [V 1.0010] – cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo[T 1.0013]. Okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo.

24. The non-disappearance condition: The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the non-disappearance condition. The four great elements are a condition for one another by way of the non-disappearance condition. At the moment of conception, name-and-form are a condition for one another by way of the non-disappearance condition. Consciousness and mental factors are a condition for materiality originated by consciousness by way of the non-disappearance condition. The great elements are a condition for derived materiality by way of the non-disappearance condition.

Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Sotāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Ghānāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Jivhāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo.

The eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The ear-base is a condition for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The nose-base is a condition for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The tongue-base is a condition for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The body-base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition.

Rūpāyatanaṃ [M 1.0010] cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Saddāyatanaṃ sotaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Gandhāyatanaṃ ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Rasāyatanaṃ jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ saddāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo.

The form-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The sound-base is a condition for the ear-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The odor-base is a condition for the nose-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The taste-base is a condition for the tongue-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The tangible-base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition. The form-base, sound-base, odor-base, taste-base, and tangible-base are a condition for the mind-element and for the states associated with it by way of the non-disappearance condition.

Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ avigatapaccayena paccayo.

That material form depending on which the mind-element and the mind-consciousness-element arise, that material form is a condition for the mind-element, for the mind-consciousness-element, and for the states associated with them by way of the non-disappearance condition.

Paccayaniddeso.

The Exposition of Conditions.

28. Siyā kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. (5) Akusalābyākatapadaṃ

(5) The Unwholesome and Indeterminate Section

29. Siyā [M 1.0012] akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā.

29. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon arises by root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon arises by root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises by root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon, wholesome and indeterminate phenomena arise by root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon, unwholesome and indeterminate phenomena arise by root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon, wholesome and unwholesome phenomena arise by root condition. It may be that, dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon, wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena arise by root condition.

(6) Kusalākusalapadaṃ

(6) The Wholesome and Unwholesome Section

30. Siyā [V 1.0013] kusalañca akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca [T 1.0017] akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca akusalo ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā.

30. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon and an unwholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon arises by root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon and an unwholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon arises by root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon and an unwholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises by root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon and an unwholesome phenomenon, wholesome and indeterminate phenomena arise by root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon and an unwholesome phenomenon, unwholesome and indeterminate phenomena arise by root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon and an unwholesome phenomenon, wholesome and unwholesome phenomena arise by root condition. It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon and an unwholesome phenomenon, wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena arise by root condition.

(7) Kusalākusalābyākatapadaṃ

(7) The Wholesome, Unwholesome, and Indeterminate Section

31. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjeyya [M 1.0013] hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca akusalo ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā. Siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā.

31. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition. An unskillful state may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition. An indeterminate state may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition. Skillful and indeterminate states may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition. Unskillful and indeterminate states may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition. Skillful and unskillful states may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition. Skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate states may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition.

Hetupaccayavāro.

The Section on the Root Condition.

32. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya ārammaṇapaccayā[T 1.0018].

32. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of object condition.

(Yathā hetupaccayo vitthārito, evaṃ ārammaṇapaccayopi vitthāretabbo vācanāmaggena.)

(Just as the root condition has been explained in detail, so too should the object condition be explained in detail by the method of recitation.)

33. Siyā [V 1.0014] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya adhipatipaccayā… anantarapaccayā… samanantarapaccayā… sahajātapaccayā… aññamaññapaccayā… nissayapaccayā… upanissayapaccayā… purejātapaccayā… pacchājātapaccayā… āsevanapaccayā… kammapaccayā… vipākapaccayā… āhārapaccayā… indriyapaccayā… jhānapaccayā… maggapaccayā… sampayuttapaccayā… vippayuttapaccayā… atthipaccayā… natthipaccayā… vigatapaccayā.

33. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of predominance condition… proximity condition… contiguity condition… co-nascence condition… mutuality condition… dependence condition… decisive support condition… pre-nascence condition… post-nascence condition… repetition condition… kamma condition… resultant condition… nutriment condition… faculty condition… jhāna condition… path condition… association condition… dissociation condition… presence condition… absence condition… disappearance condition.

34. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya avigatapaccayā…pe… akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca… abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca… kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca… akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca… kusalañca akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca… kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya… akusalo dhammo uppajjeyya… abyākato dhammo uppajjeyya… kusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ… akusalo [M 1.0014] ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ… kusalo ca akusalo ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ… kusalo ca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ avigatapaccayā.

34. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of non-disappearance condition… dependent on an unskillful state… dependent on an indeterminate state… dependent on a skillful and indeterminate state… dependent on an unskillful and indeterminate state… dependent on a skillful and unskillful state… dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state, a skillful state may arise… an unskillful state may arise… an indeterminate state may arise… skillful and indeterminate states may arise… unskillful and indeterminate states may arise… skillful and unskillful states may arise… skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate states may arise by way of non-disappearance condition.

(Yathā hetupaccayo vitthārito, evaṃ avigatapaccayopi vitthāretabbo vācanāmaggena.)

(Just as the root condition is explained in detail, so too should the non-disappearance condition be explained in detail by the method of recitation.)

Ekamūlakaṃ.

Single-rooted.

Dumūlakādi

The two-rooted and so on.

Hetumūlakaṃ

Rooted in the Root Condition.

35. Siyā [T 1.0019] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā…pe… siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā.

35. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of root condition and object condition... A skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state may arise dependent on a skillful, unskillful, and indeterminate state by way of root condition and object condition.

36. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā adhipatipaccayā [V 1.0015] …pe… hetupaccayā anantarapaccayā… hetupaccayā samanantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā avigatapaccayā.

36. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of root condition and predominance condition… by way of root condition and proximity condition… by way of root condition and contiguity condition… by way of root condition and non-disappearance condition.

Dumūlakaṃ.

Two-rooted.

37. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā anantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā avigatapaccayā.

37. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of root condition, object condition, and predominance condition… by way of root condition, object condition, and proximity condition… by way of root condition, object condition, and non-disappearance condition.

Timūlakaṃ.

Three-rooted.

38. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā anantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā avigatapaccayā.

38. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of root condition, object condition, predominance condition, and proximity condition… by way of root condition, object condition, predominance condition, and non-disappearance condition.

Catumūlakaṃ.

Four-rooted.

(Pañcamūlakādikā saṃkhittā. Ekamūlakaṃ, dumūlakaṃ, timūlakaṃ, catumūlakaṃ, pañcamūlakaṃ, sabbamūlakaṃ asammuyhantena vitthāretabbaṃ.)

(The five-rooted and so forth are condensed. The single-rooted, the two-rooted, the three-rooted, the four-rooted, the five-rooted, and the all-rooted should be explained in detail by one who is not confused.)

Hetumūlakaṃ.

Rooted in the Root Condition.

Ārammaṇamūlakādi

Rooted in the Object Condition, and so on.

39. Siyā [T 1.0020][M 1.0015] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya ārammaṇapaccayā hetupaccayā… ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā…pe… ārammaṇapaccayā avigatapaccayā.

39. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of object condition and root condition… by way of object condition and predominance condition… by way of object condition and non-disappearance condition.

Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya adhipatipaccayā… anantarapaccayā… samanantarapaccayā… sahajātapaccayā… aññamaññapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā [V 1.0016] hetupaccayā… avigatapaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā… avigatapaccayā adhipatipaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā vigatapaccayā.

A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of predominance condition… proximity condition… contiguity condition… co-nascence condition… mutuality condition… and so on… by way of non-disappearance condition and root condition… by way of non-disappearance condition and object condition… by way of non-disappearance condition and predominance condition… and so on… by way of non-disappearance condition and disappearance condition.

Dumūlakaṃ.

Two-rooted.

40. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā… avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā adhipatipaccayā… avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā anantarapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā vigatapaccayā.

40. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of non-disappearance condition, root condition, and object condition… by way of non-disappearance condition, root condition, and predominance condition… by way of non-disappearance condition, root condition, and proximity condition… and so on… by way of non-disappearance condition, root condition, and disappearance condition.

41. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā… avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā anantarapaccayā…pe… vigatapaccayā.

41. A skillful state may arise dependent on a skillful state by way of non-disappearance condition, root condition, object condition, and predominance condition… by way of non-disappearance condition, root condition, object condition, and proximity condition… and so on… up to disappearance condition.

(Ekekassa padassa ekamūlakaṃ, dumūlakaṃ, timūlakaṃ, catumūlakaṃ, pañcamūlakaṃ, sabbamūlakaṃ asammuyhantena vitthāretabbaṃ. )

(For each term, the single-rooted, two-rooted, three-rooted, four-rooted, five-rooted, and all-rooted should be explained in detail by one who is not confused.)

(Ka) tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ tikañceva dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha anulomamhi nayā sugambhīrāti.

(Ka) The triad, and the excellent Paṭṭhāna, the supreme dyad;

The pair and the triad, the triad and the pair;

The triad and the triad, the pair and the pair;

Six modes in the forward order are very profound.

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. Conditional Negation

42. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya nahetupaccayā[T 1.0021].

42. Suppose a wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state, but not by the root condition.

(Yathā [M 1.0016] anulome hetupaccayo vitthārito, evaṃ paccanīyepi nahetupaccayo vitthāretabbo.)

Just as the root condition has been elaborated in the direct order, so too should the negation of the root condition be elaborated.

43. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya naārammaṇapaccayā… naadhipatipaccayā… naanantarapaccayā… nasamanantarapaccayā… nasahajātapaccayā… naaññamaññapaccayā… nanissayapaccayā… naupanissayapaccayā… napurejātapaccayā… napacchājātapaccayā [V 1.0017] … naāsevanapaccayā… nakammapaccayā… navipākapaccayā… naāhārapaccayā… naindriyapaccayā… najhānapaccayā… namaggapaccayā… nasampayuttapaccayā… navippayuttapaccayā… noatthipaccayā… nonatthipaccayā… novigatapaccayā… noavigatapaccayā.

43. Suppose a wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state, not by the object condition... not by the dominance condition... not by the contiguity condition... not by the immediate contiguity condition... not by the conascence condition... not by the mutuality condition... not by the dependence condition... not by the strong support condition... not by the prenascence condition... not by the postnascence condition... not by the repetition condition... not by the kamma condition... not by the result condition... not by the nutriment condition... not by the faculty condition... not by the jhāna condition... not by the path condition... not by the association condition... not by the dissociation condition... not by the presence condition... not by the absence condition... not by the disappearance condition... not by the non-disappearance condition.

44. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya nahetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā….

44. Suppose a wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state, but not by the root condition, nor by the object condition.

(Yathā anulome ekekassa padassa ekamūlakaṃ, dumūlakaṃ, timūlakaṃ, catumūlakaṃ, yāva tevīsatimūlakaṃ evaṃ paccanīyepi vitthāretabbaṃ. )

Just as in the forward order, each term was expanded into single-rooted, double-rooted, triple-rooted, quadruple-rooted, up to twenty-three-rooted combinations, so too should it be expanded in the negative order.

(Kha) tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ tikañceva dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha paccanīyamhi nayā sugambhīrāti.

(Kha) The triad, the excellent Exposition, and the supreme dyad;

The pair and the triad, and the triad and the pair;

The triad and the triad, and the pair and the pair;

Six methods in the negation are very profound.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. Conditional Affirmative-Negative

45. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā… siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā.

45. Suppose a wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state, through the root condition, but not through the object condition... Suppose an unwholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state, through the root condition, but not through the object condition.

(Yathā anulome hetupaccayo vitthārito, evaṃ anulomapaccanīyepi padaṃ [T 1.0022] vitthāretabbaṃ.)

Just as the root condition was elaborated in the forward order, so too should the terms in the affirmative-negative order be elaborated.

46. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā naadhipatipaccayā… hetupaccayā naanantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā noavigatapaccayā.

46. Suppose a wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state, through the root condition but not through the dominance condition... through the root condition but not through the contiguity condition... and so on... through the root condition but not through the non-disappearance condition.

47. Siyā [M 1.0017] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā naadhipatipaccayā… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā naanantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā noavigatapaccayā.

47. Suppose a wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state, through the root condition and the object condition, but not through the dominance condition... through the root condition and the object condition, but not through the contiguity condition... and so on... through the root condition and the object condition, but not through the non-disappearance condition.

Hetupaccayā [V 1.0018] ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā naanantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā noavigatapaccayā.

Through the root condition, the object condition, and the dominance condition, but not through the contiguity condition... and so on... through the root condition, the object condition, and the dominance condition, but not through the non-disappearance condition.

Hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā anantarapaccayā nasamanantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā anantarapaccayā noavigatapaccayā…pe….

Through the root condition, the object condition, the dominance condition, and the contiguity condition, but not through the immediate contiguity condition... and so on... through the root condition, the object condition, the dominance condition, and the contiguity condition, but not through the non-disappearance condition... and so on.

Hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā anantarapaccayā samanantarapaccayā sahajātapaccayā aññamaññapaccayā nissayapaccayā upanissayapaccayā purejātapaccayā pacchājātapaccayā āsevanapaccayā kammapaccayā vipākapaccayā āhārapaccayā indriyapaccayā jhānapaccayā maggapaccayā sampayuttapaccayā vippayuttapaccayā atthipaccayā natthipaccayā vigatapaccayā noavigatapaccayā.

By the root condition, by the object condition, by the dominance condition, by the contiguity condition, by the immediate contiguity condition, by the conascence condition, by the mutuality condition, by the dependence condition, by the strong support condition, by the prenascence condition, by the postnascence condition, by the repetition condition, by the kamma condition, by the result condition, by the nutriment condition, by the faculty condition, by the jhāna condition, by the path condition, by the association condition, by the dissociation condition, by the presence condition, by the absence condition, by the disappearance condition, but not by the non-disappearance condition.

48. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya ārammaṇapaccayā… adhipatipaccayā… anantarapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā nahetupaccayā [T 1.0023]… avigatapaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā novigatapaccayā.

48. A wholesome state might arise in dependence on a wholesome state by the object condition... by the dominance condition... by the contiguity condition... and so on... by the non-disappearance condition, but not by the root condition... by the non-disappearance condition, but not by the object condition... and so on... by the non-disappearance condition, but not by the disappearance condition.

Avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā novigatapaccayā.

By the non-disappearance condition and by the root condition, but not by the object condition... and so on... by the non-disappearance condition and by the root condition, but not by the disappearance condition.

Avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā naadhipatipaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā novigatapaccayā.

By the non-disappearance condition, by the root condition, and by the object condition, but not by the dominance condition... and so on... by the non-disappearance condition, by the root condition, and by the object condition, but not by the disappearance condition.

Avigatapaccayā hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā anantarapaccayā samanantarapaccayā sahajātapaccayā…pe… novigatapaccayā.

By the non-disappearance condition, by the root condition, by the object condition, by the dominance condition, by the contiguity condition, by the immediate contiguity condition, by the conascence condition... and so on... but not by the disappearance condition.

(Ga) tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ tikañceva dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha anulomapaccanīyamhi nayā sugambhīrāti.

(Ga) The triad, and the excellent Paṭṭhāna, the supreme dyad;

The pair and the triad, the triad and the pair;

The triad and the triad, the pair and the pair;

Six methods in the affirmative-negative order are very profound.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Conditional Negative-Affirmative

49. Siyā [V 1.0019][M 1.0018] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya nahetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya nahetupaccayā adhipatipaccayā…pe… nahetupaccayā avigatapaccayā.

49. A wholesome state might arise in dependence on a wholesome state, not by the root condition, but by the object condition. A wholesome state might arise in dependence on a wholesome state, not by the root condition, but by the dominance condition… and so on… not by the root condition, but by the non-disappearance condition.

50. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya nahetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā.

50. A wholesome state might arise in dependence on a wholesome state, not by the root condition and not by the object condition, but by the dominance condition… and so on… by the non-disappearance condition.

Nahetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā naadhipatipaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā.

Not by the root condition, not by the object condition, not by the dominance condition… and so on… by the non-disappearance condition.

Nahetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā naadhipatipaccayā naanantarapaccayā nasamanantarapaccayā…pe… noatthipaccayā nonatthipaccayā novigatapaccayā avigatapaccayā.

Not by the root condition, not by the object condition, not by the dominance condition, not by the contiguity condition, not by the immediate contiguity condition… and so on… not by the presence condition, not by the absence condition, not by the disappearance condition, but by the non-disappearance condition.

51. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya naārammaṇapaccayā [T 1.0024] hetupaccayā.

51. A wholesome state might arise in dependence on a wholesome state, not by the object condition, but by the root condition.

52. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya naārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā…pe… naārammaṇapaccayā avigatapaccayā…pe… noavigatapaccayā hetupaccayā… noavigatapaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā…pe… noavigatapaccayā vigatapaccayā.

52. A wholesome state might arise in dependence on a wholesome state, not by the object condition, but by the dominance condition… and so on… not by the object condition, but by the non-disappearance condition… and so on… not by the non-disappearance condition, but by the root condition… not by the non-disappearance condition, but by the object condition… and so on… not by the non-disappearance condition, but by the disappearance condition.

Noavigatapaccayā nahetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā…pe… noavigatapaccayā nahetupaccayā vigatapaccayā.

Not by non-disappearance condition, not by root condition; by object condition… and so on… not by non-disappearance condition, not by root condition; by disappearance condition.

Noavigatapaccayā nahetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā naadhipatipaccayā…pe… noatthipaccayā nonatthipaccayā vigatapaccayā.

Not by non-disappearance condition, not by root condition, not by object condition, not by dominance condition… and so on… not by presence condition, not by absence condition; by disappearance condition.

(Gha) tikañca [V 1.0020] paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ tikañceva dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha paccanīyānulomamhi nayā sugambhīrāti.

(Gha) The triads and the supreme dyads of the excellent Paṭṭhāna; dyads and triads, and triads and dyads; triads and triads, and dyads and dyads; six methods in the Negative-Positive are very profound.

Pucchāvāro.

The Section on Questions.

Niddesavāre tevīsatipaccayā.

In the Section of Exposition, twenty-three conditions.
